cover.lead: Yayasan MENDAKI and NUS High School of Mathematics and Science sign a three-year MOU to widen access and exposure to STEM for Malay/Muslim students.

about.body: Over the next *three years,* MENDAKI and NUS High School will work together to widen access to STEM for Malay/Muslim students. NUS High School brings its expertise in mathematics, science and research, while MENDAKI brings its understanding of the community and its professional networks.

areas.title: STEM scholarships
areas.outcome: Financial support for students to pursue their interest in STEM

areas.title: Mentoring & networks
areas.outcome: Students learn from professionals in MENDAKI's networks and explore career pathways

areas.title: Enrichment & outreach
areas.outcome: More youths get to discover maths, science and technology

impact.headline: scholarships for STEM
impact.body: The Tay Eng Soon Endowment – MENDAKI Scholarship for STEM, funded by Temasek Foundation, supports Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents enrolled as full-time Year 1 students at NUS High School.

stats.label: Renewable for one year, subject to NUS High School's requirements

journey.caption: The MOU builds on MENDAKI's wider support for youths. Through Mekar Belia, about 240 students, parents and mentors visited Mediacorp, the Cross Island Line–Punggol Extension Project Information Centre, Singapore General Hospital and Universal Robots.

quote.text: As technology continues to reshape our economy and the way we work, we want more Malay/Muslim students to see STEM as a pathway that is open to them.
quote.attribution: Mr Feroz Akber, Chief Executive Officer, Yayasan MENDAKI
